claims.statement: Mota's verification is entirely vitest-based and comes in three postures: colocated unit tests (run by `pnpm test` in every workspace), API e2e tests in `apps/api/test` that boot the real Nest module through `createApp`, and Postgres integration tests gated on a present `DATABASE_URL` and run via `pnpm test:integration`.

Turbo's `test`, `typecheck`, and `test:integration` tasks all declare `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, which is a functional prerequisite rather than an optimization: `apps/api` and `packages/db` resolve `@mota/contracts` (and `apps/api` resolves `@mota/db`) through the workspace symlink and the packages' `exports` maps pointing at `./dist`, with no `paths` mapping, so those `dist` trees must exist before any Node-side test can import the shared Zod schemas.

The web app is exempt from that build prerequisite: `apps/web/vite.config.ts` aliases `@mota/contracts` and `@mota/contracts/transit-settings` directly to `packages/contracts/src`, mirrored by `compilerOptions.paths` in `apps/web/tsconfig.json`, so web tests and typechecks read the contracts TypeScript source regardless of whether the packages were built.

The `test:integration` turbo task declares `cache: false` and `env: ["DATABASE_URL"]` (plus `dependsOn: ["^build"]` and no outputs), so its result is never stored in or replayed from `.turbo/cache` and the database URL value participates in the task hash.

`createApp` in `apps/api/test/create-test-app.ts` builds the application once and memoizes it: `Test.createTestingModule` imports `AppModule.register({ ...options, upstreamFetch })`, compiles it, creates a `NestFastifyApplication` on a plain `FastifyAdapter`, calls `app.init()` and awaits `getHttpAdapter().getInstance().ready()`, then reuses that same application promise for every subsequent `request()` call — which is what lets catalog-caching tests observe one upstream call across several HTTP requests, while two `createApp()` calls yield two independent applications.

`createApp`'s `request()` drives Fastify's `inject` and wraps the result in a real `Response`: it copies inject headers into a `Headers` object (appending repeated headers individually), and constructs `new Response(response.body, { status, headers })`, enabling tests to use `response.json()`, `response.status`, and `response.headers.getSetCookie()` for multi-cookie assertions; request bodies other than `string` or `Buffer` are dropped rather than serialized, so JSON bodies are always `JSON.stringify(...)` strings.

The e2e harness is only possible because `AppModuleOptions` is the composition root: `upstreamFetch`, `verifySession`, `settingsRepository`, `oauthConfig`, `now`, `subwayArrivalUpstream`, and the transit catalog knobs (`refreshMs`, `retryMs`, warmup, minimum item counts, `random`) are all injectable through `AppModule.register`, so tests swap collaborators without patching production code.

The `AppModule.register` defaults are chosen for testability and fail-loud behavior: `warmup` defaults to `false` (no timers or warmup network), minimum catalog items default to `1` so a one-row fixture passes the completeness gate, and a missing repository or verifier throws a descriptive error (`Settings repository is not configured.` / `Supabase auth is not configured.`) instead of returning empty data — while production `main.ts` passes the opposite values (warmup on, 10,000 bus / 100 subway minimums, a real Drizzle repository).

Transit e2e tests inject a `vi.fn()` as `upstreamFetch` and treat it as an argument contract — asserting the exact upstream URL called, that `signal: expect.any(AbortSignal)` was passed (the adapters' timeouts), and the call count — while the settings e2e suite stubs `verifySession` by regexing the user id out of the `mota-access` cookie, keeping the HTTP boundary and controller logic real.

The settings e2e suite injects `MemorySettingsRepository`, a `Map`-backed implementation of `@mota/db`'s `UserSettingsRepository` interface that throws `SettingsVersionConflictError` when `expectedVersion` does not match, letting the suite prove per-user isolation, `409 SETTINGS_VERSION_CONFLICT`, and `400 INVALID_SETTINGS` with no database.

The settings suite proves two auth-failure behaviors at the HTTP boundary that a stubbed verifier alone cannot: when `verifySession` throws `SupabaseUnavailableError`, `GET /api/settings` returns `503 AUTH_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` rather than treating the user as anonymous; and when `verifySession` invokes its `onSetCookie` callback, the rotated session cookies are relayed on the settings response.

`apps/api/test/fake-supabase.ts` starts a real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port that generates a genuine ES256 keypair with `jose` and serves the public half as a JWK at `GET /auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json` under `kid: "test-key"`, `alg: "ES256"`, `use: "sig"`.

The fake Supabase handles both token grants the app uses: `POST /auth/v1/token` reads `grant_type` from the query (`pkce` and `refresh_token`) and returns a signed `access_token`, a random `refresh_token`, `expires_in: 3600`, and `token_type: bearer` — matching `SupabaseAuthClient.exchangeCode` and `.refresh`. It also records `POST /auth/v1/signout` refresh-token bodies into a `signoutRequests` array so tests can assert the exact token revoked and that anonymous logout revokes nothing.

Because the fake's keys are real, the auth e2e tests verify actual JWT semantics rather than a mocked verifier: the app fetches the JWKS over HTTP, performs real ES256 signature verification against the real issuer (`${url}/auth/v1`), audience and `role` claims, and a token minted with `expiresIn: -60` is genuinely expired and reported as anonymous. Tests inject the fake via `oauthConfig.supabaseUrl`, so issuer, JWKS, and token endpoints are all derived from the fake's address.

The same `startFakeSupabase` fake is reused by the unit-level `src/auth/supabaseJwt.test.ts`, which targets `verifyAccessToken` directly — accepting a signed token with its claims and rejecting garbage tokens as anonymous — so the unit and e2e layers share one fake identity provider.

`apps/api/vitest.config.mts` sets `environment: "node"` and includes both `src/**/*.test.ts` and `test/**/*.test.ts`. That include is what puts the Postgres integration file inside `pnpm test`, which is why the `describe.runIf` gate is load-bearing rather than dead code.

Both Postgres integration files use the same gate — `const databaseUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL; const integration = describe.runIf(Boolean(databaseUrl));` — so without `DATABASE_URL` vitest collects the file but the describe body never runs (reported skipped, not failed), keeping `pnpm test` green on a database-less machine.

`test:integration` runs exactly one named vitest file per workspace: `@mota/db` runs `src/repository.integration.test.ts` (repository-level: two uniquely-keyed users saved at version 1, `find` returning `null` for an unknown user, and a stale-version `save` rejecting with `SettingsVersionConflictError`), while `@mota/api` runs `test/settings.postgres.integration.test.ts` (the same persistence semantics through the HTTP boundary with `DrizzleUserSettingsRepository` injected and a stubbed `verifySession`).

Both integration files construct their connection with `createDatabase` — the same `postgres(..., { max: 5, prepare: false })` pool production uses — key their rows with `crypto.randomUUID()`-suffixed auth user ids (`integration-…` and `api-integration-…`) so they never collide with real users even against the shared `mota` database, and clean up in `afterAll` by deleting their rows and ending the client.

The `apps/api` transit e2e suite pins the adapter boundary invariants: nearby searches are served from one cached complete catalog (single upstream call across multiple requests), concurrent cold requests share one pending catalog load (proven by manually releasing a promise), malformed upstream rows are dropped while valid ones survive, stale cached stations are still served after the upstream fails, bus arrival lookups stay realtime rather than catalog-cached, out-of-bounds coordinates return `400` without any upstream call, and `/api/health` reports non-gating `transitCatalogs` readiness.

`apps/api/test/transit-catalog-fallback.e2e.test.ts` is the only place the bus catalog completeness-gate fallback is observable: with `minimumBusCatalogItems: 2` and a one-row upstream payload, the complete catalog is rejected and the controller falls back to the location-scoped live lookup (`kiloMeter=0.8`) instead of `kiloMeter=45`.

The auth e2e suite encodes the full OAuth/session contract: PKCE redirect URL parameters (`provider=google`, `prompt=select_account`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, a state-carrying `redirect_to`), three host-only flow cookies (`Max-Age=600`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, no `Domain`), cross-site `return_to` rejection, the callback exchange setting five cookies (two session plus three cleared flow), state-mismatch rejection with `401`, logout clearing cookies and revoking server-side, and refresh-cookie rotation setting new access and refresh cookies.

The colocated unit tests pin the pure contracts: `pkce.test.ts` (base64url verifier/state shape, RFC 7636 appendix B S256 vector), `sessionCookies.test.ts` (`__Host-` prefixing only for https origins, `Max-Age`/`HttpOnly`/`SameSite=Lax` serialization, never a `Domain` attribute, cookie header parsing), `env.test.ts` (`loadEnv` defaults, `DATABASE_*` URL encoding, startup failure without database or Supabase credentials), `transitSettings.test.ts` (legacy selection-document migration into both commute contexts, singular-id to one-element list, dedupe, and the `MAX_SELECTED_BUS_STOPS` cap), and `schema.test.ts` (`user_settings` name, exact four-column order, `auth_user_id` as the inline primary key).

`managedCatalog.test.ts` pins the catalog state machine in isolation — single-flight cold load shared across concurrent readers, atomic snapshot swap when a refresh becomes due, stale data kept when a refresh fails, and, under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, that the proactive refresh timer fires and is cleared by `stop()` leaving zero timers.

Web tests are colocated as `*.test.tsx` next to their sources (`src/App.test.tsx`, `src/components/*.test.tsx`, `src/hooks/*.test.tsx`) with a per-file `@vitest-environment jsdom` docblock; `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` declares no `include` (vitest default discovery) but sets `setupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]` and `clearMocks: true`, and the setup registers `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` and unmounts the tree in an `afterEach` cleanup.

`apps/web/src/App.test.tsx` uses a `vi.hoisted` mutable `mediaQueryState` object shared with a `vi.mock` factory that replaces `useMediaQuery` with `() => mediaQueryState.matches`; flipping `mediaQueryState.matches` inside a test switches `App`'s `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 960px)")` between the desktop and mobile layouts without needing a jsdom `matchMedia` implementation.

The web suites mock only the leaves of the tree and keep the rest real: `App.test.tsx` replaces `MapStage` with a `data-*` section stub exposing test buttons, stubs `useAuthSession` to a static anonymous session, and partially mocks `./api/client` via `importOriginal` so only `fetchArrivals`/`fetchSubwayArrivals` become spies; `MapStage.test.tsx` stubs `MapCanvas`; `MapCanvas.test.tsx` stubs `react-leaflet` with a hand-built fake map; `useAuthSession.test.tsx` uses `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", …)` and `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`. Assertions query by role and accessible name.

There is no browser e2e coverage: `apps/web/package.json` declares `"test:e2e": "playwright test"` and `@playwright/test` as a devDependency, and the root `package.json` forwards `pnpm test:e2e` to it, but the repository contains no Playwright config and no spec file, so the script as written cannot pass — end-to-end coverage comes from the API e2e layer plus the jsdom component suites.

There is no CI pipeline running the tests: the only GitHub workflow is the scheduled OpenWiki documentation update, so the README's verification list (`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration`, `pnpm build`) is a set of local commands executed only by whoever runs them.

The e2e suites are typechecked and linted alongside production code: `apps/api/tsconfig.json` includes `test`, and its `check` script lints `src test vitest.config.mts`, while `packages/*/tsconfig.build.json` exclude `*.test.ts` so no test is emitted into `dist`.
